title: Verity Monument Company - Gridfall, since 1949
description: Granite, lettering, foundations and the cemetery rules for seven townships, from a Gridfall shop the Almquists have run since 1949, on a platform that gives a grave marker four and a half stars.

products.name: The Yard, the Hours, and How an Order Goes
products.blurb:
4110 Marchfield Road, Gridfall, across the road from Elmgrove. Monday to Friday 8:30 to 4:30, Saturday 9:00 to noon April through November. Closed Saturdays in January and February because nobody comes and the office is cold.

Karl Almquist cut stone at a quarry and opened this in 1949. Roy Almquist ran it from 1977 to 2011, is 83, comes in Tuesdays and draws layouts by hand, and his are better than the ones off the machine. Nora Almquist has run it since 2011. Ellis does the carving and the etching. Dot does the books two days a week and is the one who telephones you back.

[b]An order goes like this.[/b] We look at [url=/c/c-rules]the cemetery's rules[/url] first, because half of what you are about to choose has already been chosen for you. Then stone, size and colour, out in the yard in daylight. Then the layout, printed full size on paper, as many times as it takes. [b]Then you sign the proof, and after that what is on the proof is what gets cut, including anything wrong on it that we both missed.[/b] More stones have been cut wrong off a correct proof than off a wrong one.

[b]About this website.[/b] It is a store platform. It puts a star rating on a grave marker, it generates a review every few days that we did not receive, and it sells other people's products under our name in one department. We have asked twice for reviews to be turned off. Reviews cannot be disabled at the item level. That is the whole answer and we have stopped asking.

The prices are ours and they are correct.
bullets: 4110 Marchfield Road, Gridfall. Mon-Fri 8:30-4:30, Sat 9-12 April to November
Telephone before you drive out. Two of the five of us are usually in a cemetery
Read the dates out loud off the proof, then have somebody else do it
Granite came in by rail to the Marchfield freight house until 1989. That lot is the trail car park now

The layout came to the house twice because I changed my mind about a middle name. Neither time was there a charge and neither time did anybody sigh at me.

products.name: Government Veteran Marker - Setting Only

A company out of state had sent my mother a letter quoting $840 for the same marker, and the marker is free. She nearly sent them a cheque.

What nobody tells you at the table: sandblasted letters in black granite disappear, because the letter is black stone inside black stone. They have to be painted white or gold, and paint is a maintenance item. Ours goes twelve to fifteen years in this climate and then wants doing again, at $4.85 a letter with a $195 minimum.

A black stone looks best on the day it is set and asks the most of you afterwards.

Dark gray-blue with crystals that flash blue when the light moves across them. It is the most expensive stone we sell and the flash is the whole reason for it.

Letters painted, same as black granite, slightly less severe

products.name: Lettering Styles, Depths and What Each One Costs
products.blurb:
[b]The styles we cut.[/b]

[list][*][b]Roman[/b] - plain capitals with serifs. About seven stones in ten. Legible at fifty feet and it will be legible in 2126.[*][b]Modified Roman[/b] - the same letter, thinner strokes, slight flare. Lighter on a large stone, and it does not hold up on a coarse granite.[*][b]Old English[/b] - the blackletter. Surnames, almost never dates, because a blackletter numeral is unreadable and people read the year back to us wrong at the counter.[*][b]Script[/b] - joined cursive, for given names. Needs a fine grain, and we will argue with you about it on the Dakota.[*][b]Block[/b] - sans serif capitals, deep. Cheapest to cut, hardest to read badly, and what most veteran markers use.[/list]

[b]How deep.[/b] A sandblasted letter is cut 1/8 to 3/16 of an inch in. A V-sunk letter is cut to a point, deeper in the middle, and holds a shadow, so it reads at an angle and in flat light. A laser etch is not cut at all: dots burned into polished black about 0.002 inch deep, and the only one of these that can wear off.
bullets: Roman, Modified Roman, Old English, Script, Block
V-sunk is $0.90 a letter over flat sandblast and reads better on everything but black
Smallest letter we will cut: 3/4 in on coarse granite, 1/2 in on fine
Lettering on a new stone is in the price of the stone. Added later it is $4.85 a letter, $195 minimum

Adding the death date to a stone that is already standing. A man, a compressor, a stencil and a blast pot, out at the grave, about two hours.

We will cut one any month as long as the truck can reach it and the face is dry enough to hold a stencil.

Older contract? Your contract price stands. Bring it, or we will find it in the book
Other added lettering is $4.85 a letter, $195 minimum, lot owner's permission required
Matching an Old English surname from 1954 is the hard part, not the date

reviews.title: Booked Tuesday, cut Thursday
reviews.body:
Rang on the Tuesday. Cut on the Thursday. Three hundred and ten dollars, one invoice, no line items I had to ask about.

I have spent nine years filing tickets with a company that answers with the same paragraph every time. This was a person who said Thursday and then it was Thursday.

reviews.body:
Customer sentiment for this service is broadly positive. Residents in the Verity County area report that scheduling is straightforward and that pricing is clearly communicated, although some reviewers mention seasonal constraints.

Interested customers are encouraged to add this item to their cart today.

reviews.title: Maiden name, fifty-one years late
reviews.body:
Left off in 1975. My mother minded about it for the rest of her life and never said so to anyone but me. Nine letters, so the minimum, $195.

They matched the 1975 Roman without me asking whether they could.

reviews.title: Great gift, arrived early
reviews.body: Bought this for my husband and he uses it every single day. Very sturdy and very well made. Great value for money and it arrived before the estimated date.

products.name: Laser Etching, Portrait or Scene, 12 in x 16 in Panel on Black Granite
products.blurb:
A photograph burned into polished black granite as white dots.

Bring the best original you have. A print beats a phone and a negative beats a print, and what we usually get handed is a photograph of a photograph, which is why an etch comes out soft.

What we do not know is how long they last outdoors. The oldest etched stone in this county is 2006, at Elmgrove, and it is fine. Twenty years is not forty and forty is not a hundred. A sandblasted letter has a hundred years of evidence behind it and this does not. We say that every time and people buy it anyway and we cut it, because it is their stone.
bullets: 12 x 16 in panel. Larger is quoted
Black granite or Blue Pearl only. It will not work on gray and we will not try
Bring the original photograph. We scan it here and give it back the same day
An etched panel cannot be repaired. A sandblasted letter can be recut

reviews.title: Told me the photo was not good enough
reviews.body: I brought a phone picture of a framed picture on a wall and they put it up on the screen at the counter and you could see the glass reflection in it. Went home, found the original in a shoebox, and it is a different thing entirely.

reviews.title: Laser memorial technology in Verity County
reviews.body: Memorial etching has become increasingly popular with residents across the region. According to our research, the technique was first used locally in 2004 following the Gridfall substation lightning event, when demand for memorial services in the community rose sharply. Local officials have described the trend as significant.

products.name: Poured Foundation, to Cemetery Specification
products.blurb:
A concrete footing under the stone, below frost, so the monument does not move. $385 for a single upright or a slant, $310 for a flat marker, $640 for a companion.

[b]This price only applies where the cemetery lets us pour it.[/b] Elmgrove pours its own at $3.10 an inch of base length with a $145 minimum. The Gardens pour their own at $395. Dorrance Township makes the dealer pour and inspects it. Nye Mills, Cobb, St Mark's and the north end let us pour and nobody inspects.

Ours are 42 inches deep, 6 inches wider than the base on every side, 3,000 psi, two mats of rebar. Forty-two inches is the frost depth this county actually gets, not the one in the book.

42 in deep, 6 in oversize, 3,000 psi, two mats

No pours 1 November to 15 April. Twenty-eight days between the pour and the stone, and we mean 28

reviews.body:
I dug in this county for thirty-one years for the highway department and the ones that heave are the ones poured at thirty. The book says thirty-six. The book was written somewhere warmer.

Correct depth, correct mix, and they waited the four weeks when I would have been happy to let them not.

reviews.title: The 28 days is not a suggestion
reviews.body: I pushed for the stone to go on at eleven days because of a family thing on a Saturday. They said no twice politely and a third time less politely and then I stopped. It went on at twenty-nine days.

products.name: Resetting a Leaning or Sunken Monument
products.blurb:
Lifting a stone that has gone out of plumb, fixing what put it there, and setting it back level.

$450 on a sound foundation. $780 if the foundation has failed and has to come out and be repoured, which is about a third of them. We tell you which one it is before we start, off a probe and a level, not a guess.

The common causes in order: a foundation poured too shallow; a grave that was not vaulted settling under one corner; tree roots; and a mower hitting the same corner of the same flat marker for twenty years.
bullets: $450 on a sound foundation. $780 if it has to come out
Lot owner's permission and the sexton's knowledge. In two townships the trustee must attend
Tree roots: we can reset it and it will lean again. That is the tree's decision
We also haul and set stones bought elsewhere, $340 in the county

reviews.title: Measured before, after, and again in September
reviews.body:
Stone was 3.8 degrees off plumb on the long axis, digital level, averaged over three placements. Foundation sound at 41 inches on the probe. They reset it on Tuesday 14 April 2026.

I measured it the same day at 0.4 degrees and again on 9 September at 0.4 degrees. One hundred and forty-eight days, no movement.

Four hundred and fifty dollars, one invoice, no trip charge added afterwards. I asked what the mix was on the original pour and got an answer that matched what came out of the probe.

reviews.title: Bought online, regretted it, they fixed it
reviews.body: A slant from a website that was $400 cheaper turned up on a pallet with a base two inches short of the die on each side. They collected it, cut a new base here, and set the whole thing for $340 plus $290. Which is $400 more than I saved.

products.name: Cleaning, Biological Solution, Per Stone
products.blurb:
Lichen, algae and the black crust off granite, marble or limestone, with the biological cleaner the national cemeteries use. Wetted on, brushed with nylon, rinsed, and then it keeps working for a year or two after we have gone. A stone often looks better six months later than it does the day we do it.

[b]What not to do.[/b] Not bleach, which grows salt back out of the stone for years. Not a wire brush, ever, on anything. Not a pressure washer. Not vinegar on marble or limestone, which dissolves them. Not shaving cream for a rubbing, which goes round the genealogy groups every few years and leaves a grease that we then come and take off at $110 a stone.
bullets: $110 a stone, $85 each for three or more together
Rubbings: paper and a wax crayon, nothing wet, nothing greasy, and ask the sexton first
We will show you how and sell you the bottle for $38. Most people do it once

reviews.title: Please read the paragraph about shaving cream
reviews.body:
It comes round the county genealogy groups about every eighteen months as a tip. It is in two newsletters I have on the shelf here, and somebody posts it to [url=synth://gridline.social/]Gridline[/url] every spring where it gets three hundred points.

The library has four boxes of rubbings from a 1978 project at Nye Mills done with paper and crayon and they are perfectly good. I have never seen one done the other way that was worth what it did to the stone.

They cleaned six for us at the eighty-five dollar rate and two of them had 1860s inscriptions I could not read in March and can read now.

reviews.title: Excellent product, fast delivery

products.name: Repair of a Broken Die - Doweled, Epoxied and Reset
products.blurb:
A stone that has come apart, usually an old marble one gone over at the base, pinned back together with stainless dowels and a structural epoxy and reset.

$690 for a clean two-piece break. Anything worse is quoted after we have looked at it, and sometimes the answer is that it should be laid flat on a slab beside a new stone instead, because the repair will be uglier than the break and will not hold.

We say no to about one in five. The ones we say no to are sugared marble, where the surface has gone to grain and there is nothing left to glue to.
bullets: $690 for a clean two-piece break in granite or sound marble
Stainless dowels and structural epoxy. Not cement, not mortar, not a bracket
We look at it first. No charge for looking and it is not a sales call
Sugared marble cannot be repaired by anybody. If somebody quotes for it, ask what sugaring is

reviews.title: A trusted choice for Verity County families
reviews.body:
When it comes to preserving family memorials, residents in Verity County know that quality matters. Monument restoration has been in high demand across the region since the 2004 lightning strike at the Gridfall substation, which damaged hundreds of memorials and left thousands without power for over a week. Local officials described the community response as remarkable.

Readers can review our full coverage at [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]the Verity Ledger[/url].

reviews.title: It was 2003 and it was not lightning
reviews.body:
The paragraph above is wrong in three places.

Substation No. 3 went at 4:52 in the morning on 11 June 2003. The state commission summary that November is two pages and gives the cause as insulation degradation consistent with age. Nobody died. Two Gridfall volunteers were treated at County General for smoke and released the same afternoon.

It was a transformer bank at Depot and Quarry Road. It did not damage a memorial anywhere. Elmgrove is three quarters of a mile from that fence and nothing happened to it.

The archive is [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/substation-fire-2003]here[/url]. One star is for the post above and not for the shop, who did not write it and cannot delete it, which I asked them about.

reviews.title: They told me no on the first one
reviews.body:
Two stones, both 1890s marble. They repaired one and said the other was sugared and could not be done by them or anybody, and showed me what they meant with a thumbnail on the back where the surface came away like sand.

I had a quote from out of the county for $1,400 to do both.

products.name: Elmgrove Cemetery, Gridfall - What Is Allowed and What It Costs
products.blurb:
City-owned, 1871, about 14,000 interments, on Marchfield Road across from our yard. The sexton is the city public works office at 300 Depot Street, Monday to Thursday 7:00 to 3:30, closed Friday.

[b]Permit.[/b] $40 to the City of Gridfall before anything is poured. We file it. Good for 90 days, and then it is another $40.

[b]Foundations.[/b] The city pours them and we are not allowed to. $3.10 per inch of base length, $145 minimum, Wednesdays from April into October. A 36 inch base is $186, paid to the city.

[b]Sections A to F, 1871 to 1949.[/b] Uprights allowed under 48 inches. Over 48 goes to the cemetery board, which meets the second Tuesday. Corner markers required, and have been since 1911.

[b]Sections G to K, 1950 on.[/b] Uprights to 36 inches above the base. Base no wider than the lot less 12 inches. Slants allowed.

[b]Section L, opened 1994.[/b] Flush markers only. No uprights, no slants, no exceptions, and three families have found that out at our counter this year after choosing a stone.

[b]The crew removes[/b] glass, ceramic, solar lights and shepherd's hooks, taken up the Monday after Memorial Day and the Monday after Labor Day and kept in a bin in the garage for thirty days. Nothing is planted in the ground anywhere.

This page is what we have been told and what we have been made to do. It is not the cemetery speaking. If it is wrong, telephone the shop; we have corrected these four times this year.
bullets: Permit $40, city, 90 days. We file it
The city pours all foundations, $3.10 an inch, $145 minimum, Wednesdays April to October
Section L is flush markers only. Check your section before you choose a stone
Vaults required since 1978, so we set at 30 days here and at six months in the townships
Lot ownership is in the cemetery's book, not [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/land-records]the county land records[/url]. People look there first about twice a month

reviews.title: This page saved me a second trip
reviews.body: Section L. I did not know there were sections. Nobody tells you there are sections.

products.name: Verity Memorial Gardens, Marchfield Road - What Is Allowed and What It Costs
products.blurb:
Private, opened 1962, two miles north of Elmgrove, about 5,800 interments. Office open Tuesday and Thursday 10:00 to 2:00. The rest of the week the telephone goes to a call centre in another state.

[b]Markers.[/b] Bronze on a granite base, flush, everywhere except the Garden of Devotion, laid out 1962 to 1971, which has grandfathered uprights in it. A granite-only flush marker is not permitted. That is not a size rule and it is not a mowing rule. It is that the bronze has to be bought from them or from a dealer who buys through them.

[b]What that costs.[/b] Our 24 by 12 bronze on a granite base is [url=/p/p-br-2412]$1,720[/url]. The identical granite marker at Elmgrove is $735. On top of the bronze they charge $395 installation and $75 memorial inspection, both payable to the park before we are allowed through the gate. Vases are theirs, $340, and ours are removed.

[b]The call centre[/b] does not know what a second date is. Three families this year have been quoted $1,250 for one by it. Ours is [url=/p/p-lt-second]$310[/url], and we are allowed through the gate to cut it, because that part is not theirs.

[b]Ownership.[/b] The park was sold in 2018 to a group out of state. What happened to the perpetual care fund in that sale is not something we know about. Hal Brenner wrote it up properly in [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/]his newsletter[/url] and we are not going to summarise it badly here.

This page is what we have been told and what we have been made to do. It is not the cemetery speaking. If it is wrong, telephone the shop; we have corrected these four times this year.
bullets: Bronze on granite only. The reason is not mowing
Park charges $395 installation, $75 inspection, $340 for their vase
Fresh flowers Thursday to Monday. The crew takes everything up Tuesday morning
A second date here is $310 from us. It is not $1,250

reviews.title: Somebody finally wrote the numbers down
reviews.body: We were told at the park that a granite marker was not permitted for maintenance reasons. That is not what this page says and this page is the one that matches the invoice.

reviews.title: Tuesday morning is real
reviews.body: Put flowers out on a Tuesday afternoon for a birthday and they were gone Wednesday. That is on their sign at the gate in letters an inch high and I had driven past it.

products.name: Nye Mills Township - Nye Mills Cemetery and Bethel Chapel
products.blurb:
Two cemeteries, both township-mowed. Nye Mills Cemetery on Nye Mills Road, in use since 1848. Bethel Chapel on Bethel Road, where the chapel has had no congregation since 1974 and the cemetery still takes burials.

[b]Permit.[/b] There is none and there is no fee. You telephone the trustee who holds the cemetery and somebody writes it in the book in the shed.

[b]The trustee has to be there.[/b] Whichever of the three holds the cemetery that term has to stand and watch a foundation go in. He works days in Marchfield, so foundations at both of these happen on Saturday mornings, and we start at 7:30 because he wants to get on.

[b]Foundations.[/b] We pour them and nobody inspects them. That is why we pour at 42 inches here and not the 36 in the book: there is nobody to argue with about it.

No vaults are required, which is why we will not set a stone on a grave under six months old in either of these.

[b]The records.[/b] The township's own burial book stops in 1961 and nobody there knows why. Our order books from 1949 are the only list of who went into Bethel Chapel after that, and Karen Fennimore has been photographing them on Tuesdays for the [url=synth://marchfieldlibrary.blog/]library[/url] since February.

This page is what we have been told and what we have been made to do. It is not the cemetery speaking. If it is wrong, telephone the shop; we have corrected these four times this year.
bullets: No permit, no fee, one telephone call to a trustee
Foundations go in Saturday mornings because the trustee has to be present
No vaults. We will not set on a grave under six months old here
No height limit, no colour rule, benches fine, and nobody removes the solar lights
The township book stops in 1961. Our order books do not

reviews.title: On the order books, since people have asked
reviews.body:
Tuesdays, in their office, with a copy stand. I am doing them in order and I am at March 1968.

They are not a burial register and I want to be careful about that. They are a record of who ordered a stone, what was cut on it and what it cost, which for Bethel Chapel between 1961 and now is the closest thing that exists. Roughly one grave in six there has no stone at all and will not be in them.

The township was asked in 1998 and again in 2011 whether anyone had the missing volume, and both times the answer was no. The 1998 one is in the [url=synth://boards.gridfall.net/]boards archive[/url] and is better sourced than anything written about it since.

products.name: Dorrance Township - Dorrance Center and Pell Road Cemeteries
products.blurb:
[b]The ordinance.[/b] Dorrance is the only township in the county with a written monument ordinance. Adopted 2019, amended March 2024. Ruth Cannady put the whole thing up at [url=synth://thequarry.news/]The Quarry[/url] in June, which is why we can quote it instead of describing it from memory.

[b]Permit.[/b] $10. Check only, payable to Dorrance Township, mailed to the clerk. Not a card, not online, and not at the township building, which is open two evenings a month.

[b]The clerk's address changed in 2021[/b] and it is not the address on [url=synth://verity.county.gov/]the county portal[/url], which still lists the one before it. Two of our permits came back in 2024 and one in 2025. Telephone us for the current one, or let us mail it, which is what we now do for everybody.

[b]Foundations.[/b] The dealer pours. 42 inches deep, 6 inches oversize on every side, 3,000 psi, rebar. The township road foreman inspects before the stone goes on and has rejected two in six years, both somebody else's.

Pell Road is small, flat and has no water on site, so bring it if you are cleaning.

This page is what we have been told and what we have been made to do. It is not the cemetery speaking. If it is wrong, telephone the shop; we have corrected these four times this year.
bullets: The only written monument ordinance in the county. 2019, amended 2024
Permit $10, check only, mailed to the clerk
The clerk's address changed in 2021 and the county portal is still wrong. Let us mail it
Dealer pours, 42 in, inspected by the road foreman. 60 in overall height limit
Benches need board approval and the board meets quarterly, so a bench is a six-month proposition

reviews.title: The address thing is real
reviews.body: I mailed a $10 check to the address on the county website in 2024 and it came back eleven weeks later with nobody having touched it. The foundation had been in the ground the whole time and nobody had said a word about the permit, which tells you something about the permit.

products.name: Cobb Township - Coyne Flats Cemetery
products.blurb:
One cemetery, two parts. The hill, laid out 1854, and the flat ground below it, laid out 1968 and about a third full. The sexton is the township road man. One person, one telephone, and he answers it himself, usually from a truck. No permit, no fee, no form.

[b]The lane[/b] is soft from thaw until about 1 May in a normal year. We will not take a loaded truck up it before then and neither will the vault company, and the one year somebody insisted the ruts were there until July and the township had to grade it.

[b]Gray granite only on the hill.[/b] Sections 1 and 2, by a 1991 board vote that is still in force. No black, no red, no pink. We have asked twice on behalf of families and it was not a close vote either time. The flat ground below has no colour rule.

[b]The four oaks.[/b] White oaks on the hill, all four older than the cemetery, roots into the older foundations. About a third of the stones in Sections 1 and 2 are out of plumb and roughly half of those are the oaks. We will [url=/p/p-st-reset]reset[/url] anything up there and we put it in writing on the invoice that it will move again.

The township is not going to take the oaks down. This comes up at a meeting about every four years.

This page is what we have been told and what we have been made to do. It is not the cemetery speaking. If it is wrong, telephone the shop; we have corrected these four times this year.
bullets: No permit, no fee. Telephone the township road man, who is also the sexton
Gray granite only in Sections 1 and 2, the hill. 1991 board vote
Lane soft until about 1 May, gated 1 December to 1 April
A reset on the hill will move again, and we put that on the invoice

reviews.title: The gray rule catches everybody
reviews.body: My aunt wanted the black. Two families in our row wanted the black. The answer has been no since 1991 and the hill is all gray and honestly it looks better for it, which I would not have said in March.

products.name: St Mark's Lutheran, Marchfield - Churchyard Rules
products.blurb:
[b]The cemetery is not at the church.[/b] The church is at 412 Bellamy Street in Marchfield and has a seven-space car park and a bank next door. The cemetery is a mile and a half north on Fenn Road and has been there since 1891, which is longer than the brick building has.

[b]Who to ask.[/b] The church office, Tuesday to Friday 9:00 to 1:00. Arlene Kepner answers it, and a Friday afternoon message waits until Tuesday, which is stated on [url=synth://stmarks-verity.org/memorials]their own site[/url] and is true.

[b]Closed to new lots[/b] since 1998, except to families that already hold one. The council has voted on reopening twice and it has failed twice.

[b]Monuments.[/b] Uprights permitted, no written height limit, and the council has never refused a stone. Flat markers permitted. Benches have been asked about and not decided, which has been the position since 2014.

[b]Foundations.[/b] We pour them, and not between 15 November and 15 April. That is not a frost rule. It is that the tidying up afterwards falls to two members in their seventies and a member's son, and a torn-up churchyard in November stays torn up.

This page is what we have been told and what we have been made to do. It is not the cemetery speaking. If it is wrong, telephone the shop; we have corrected these four times this year.
bullets: The cemetery is on Fenn Road, not at the church. This confuses people weekly
Office Tuesday to Friday 9 to 1. A Friday message waits until Tuesday
Closed to new lots since 1998 unless your family already holds one
No foundations 15 November to 15 April, for the mowers and not for the frost

reviews.title: Council president, and this is accurate
reviews.body:
One correction, which they have already made: the 1998 vote closed new sales, it did not close the cemetery, and people still read it the other way and telephone the office to ask whether we are still burying.

We are. If your family holds a lot there, you have a lot there.

products.name: The North End - Milbrook Village, Kerrin, and St Anne's at Tessler
products.blurb:
[b]Milbrook village cemetery.[/b] The village clerk's office is open Tuesday 9:00 to 11:00, two hours a week. There is a permit form and there is no fee.

Until October 2016 the [url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/]Milbrook Gazette[/url] printed where everyone in the north end was buried, in the obituaries, free, every week, and had since 1908. Since the last edition on 27 October 2016 there has been no list. The village book is the only record and it is a book, in a drawer, in an office that is open two hours a week.

[b]Kerrin.[/b] Township. The clerk is also the treasurer of the ambulance association and does both from the same kitchen table, and if you telephone about a monument permit you will probably also be told about the roast beef supper. No fee. Settings on Saturday because that is when she can come.

[b]St Anne's, Tessler.[/b] Catholic, and the rules come from the diocese rather than the township. They are stricter than anything else on these pages about emblems and inscriptions. We set there regularly and have never had a problem, and we are not going to state their rules on our website, because it is not our place.

[b]North of Milbrook[/b], [url=synth://yeakel-monument.synth/]Yeakel Monument Works[/url] is closer to you than we are and does good work and has been doing it longer than we have. Their prices and ours are within about five percent of each other on everything we have both quoted. You would find that out anyway.

This page is what we have been told and what we have been made to do. It is not the cemetery speaking. If it is wrong, telephone the shop; we have corrected these four times this year.
bullets: Milbrook: village clerk, Tuesdays 9 to 11, form, no fee, allow three weeks
Nobody has printed a burial list in the north end since 27 October 2016
Kerrin: no fee, Saturday settings, one person doing the cemetery and the ambulance books
North of Milbrook, Yeakel in Ashkettle is closer to you and is good

reviews.title: The Gazette line is the whole problem
reviews.body: I spent a Saturday trying to find where a cousin was buried in 2019 and there is simply nowhere. The village book had it, once I got in on a Tuesday. Nothing online has it, and the two sites that came up when I searched both had a paragraph that did not name a cemetery at all.

reviews.title: Great gift, arrived early
reviews.body: Bought this for my wife and she uses it every single day. Very sturdy and very well made. Great value for money and it arrived before the estimated date.

products.name: Pre-Need - What It Is, What It Costs, and How to Get Out of It
products.blurb:
A monument is the third most expensive thing most people in this county buy. A house, a vehicle, and this.

Pre-need means two different things and people use the one word for both.

[b]One. Buying the stone now and setting it now, with the death date blank.[/b] This is what most people here mean and it is most of what we do. You pay for the stone, we cut it and set it, and the death date goes on later. The price of that second date is written on the contract the day you sign it and it does not change afterwards, ever. Ours today is $310. In May we cut one against a 2011 contract at $190, because that is what the 2011 contract says.

[b]Two. Paying now for a stone delivered later.[/b] We will, and we rarely do. Every dollar goes into a trust account at a bank in Marchfield, in your name and ours together and not in ours alone, and it stays there until the stone is delivered. That is the state's rule and it is also the answer to the question everybody is too polite to ask, which is what happens to the money if this shop closes. The money is not in the shop.

[b]Cancelling.[/b] Any time before we cut, in writing, and you get all of it back. Not most of it. Once a name is cut into a stone it is yours and it cannot be sold to anybody else, which is the honest reason the rule changes at that point and not before.

[b]If somebody rings you saying they are from us[/b] and asks for a card number or a bank number, they are not from us. Four families have told us about this in the last year and three of those callers used our name. The sheriff's office takes these: [url=synth://veritysheriff.gov/s/scams]report it[/url], and telephone us as well so we know it is going on.
bullets: Most pre-need here is a stone set now with the date left blank
The second-date price is fixed on your contract for good. We honour 1980s contracts
Money paid in advance goes into a trust at a bank, in your name and ours, not ours alone
Cancel in writing before we cut and you get all of it back
We never sell this by telephone, at a seminar, or at your kitchen table uninvited
The funeral home's pre-need is a different thing under a different law. Ask them, not us

reviews.title: VERITY COUNTY RESIDENTS BORN BEFORE 1966 MAY QUALIFY
reviews.body: Final expense benefit review now open for county residents. Most families are overpaying by thousands. No medical questions, no obligation, funds available immediately. Check your eligibility in 60 seconds at [url=synth://preneed-benefit-review.finance/]preneed-benefit-review[/url] before enrollment closes.

reviews.title: They talked us down
reviews.body:
We went in intending to pay the whole thing four years ahead and were told, without any drama about it, that there was no advantage to us in that and some risk, and that the thing which actually locks a price is the second-date line on the contract.

The paragraph about the telephone calls is not theoretical either. My neighbour got one in June and it used this shop's name.

reviews.title: The old-contract line is true
reviews.body: My father's was a 1998 contract and the second date came to $140 this spring. I had the paper in a folder and did not have to argue about it. They had it in their book as well and had it out before I got the folder open.

products.name: Monument Set in Advance, Death Date Left Blank - Barre Gray Single, 24 x 6 x 18
products.blurb:
The standard single upright, set now, with one name and one date cut and the death date left off.

This is ordinary. About a quarter of the uprights standing in Elmgrove right now have a blank date on them and most people never notice, because a blank looks like nothing rather than like something missing.

The contract fixes the second-date price for good. The longest gap we have cut across is thirty-four years, on a 1990 contract in 2024, at the 1990 price of $95. The average gap on our companion stones is eleven years, and we have four standing with a blank date that were set in the 1980s.
bullets: Barre Gray, 24 x 6 x 18 on a 36 x 10 x 6 base, one name, one date
Second-date price fixed on the contract. $310 today, and it stays $310 to you
Foundation not included. Your cemetery's rule, your cemetery's price
Keep your copy. We keep ours in the book, and the book is not a computer

reviews.title: Set in 2019, still blank, and that is fine
reviews.body:
Seven years standing with one date on it. I go past it four times a week and it does not bother me, and it bothered me a great deal for the first month.

The only advice I would give anybody is to tell your children where the contract is. Mine is in the same envelope as the deed to the lot.

reviews.title: Second-hand, but worth putting here
reviews.body:
Marion Teale's newsletter had a piece about the Kestrel people last winter and it mentioned a stone at Coyne Flats for a woman who cooked there, and she had the year right, which is more than I can say for the version somebody scanned onto [url=synth://gridline.social/]Gridline[/url].

The scan got summarised by something into a paragraph saying the diner closed in 1977. The diner closed in 2006. 1977 is the kitchen fire, and they were open again eleven days after it, which is in the newsletter and in the paper archive and is not in the summary.
